Area.evidence_source: According to Searle (1979, p. viii), there are five primary ways of using speech to perform an action: assertive speech acts tell people how things are ('The sky is blue'); directives are a means of trying to get others to do things ('Please sit down'); commissives are statements of intent and commit us to actions ('I am going to kill myself'); expressives convey our feelings and attitudes ('I'm feeling sad'), and declarations bring about changes in the status quo ('I pronounce you husband and wife'). Knizek and Hjelmeland (2007) have incorporated this classification into a model of suicidal behaviour as communication. Likewise, we draw on speech act theory in our analysis of SCEs.
